message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long weekends that occur in Canada in 2023** (i.e., holidays that fall on a Friday or Monday, or are observed on a Monday when they land on a weekend).  
For each entry you’ll see the holiday name, the actual date in 2023, and the full Saturday‑to‑Monday stretch that gives you a three‑day break.

| # | Holiday | 2023 Date | Observed (if different) | Long‑Weekend Span (Sat‑Mon) |
|---|---------|-----------|--------------------------|-----------------------------|
| 1 | New Year’s Day | **Sunday Jan 1** | Observed **Mon Jan 2** | **Sat Dec 31 – Mon Jan 2** |
| 2 | Good Friday | **Friday Apr 7** | – | **Fri Apr 7 – Sun Apr 9** |
| 3 | Victoria Day | **Monday May 22** | – | **Sat May 20 – Mon May 22** |
| 4 | Canada Day | **Saturday Jul 1** | Observed **Mon Jul 3** | **Sat Jul 1 – Mon Jul 3** |
| 5 | Labour Day | **Monday Sep 4** | – | **Sat Sep 2 – Mon Sep 4** |
| 6 | Thanksgiving | **Monday Oct 9** | – | **Sat Oct 7 – Mon Oct 9** |
| 7 | Christmas | **Monday Dec 25** | – | **Sat Dec 23 – Mon Dec 25** |

> **Note:**  
> • Boxing Day (Dec 26) falls on a Tuesday in 2023, so it does **not** create a long weekend.  
> • Some provinces have additional holidays that create long weekends (e.g., Family Day on Feb 20, St. Patrick’s Day on Mar 17 in Ontario, St. George’s Day on Mar 17 in BC). Those are *not* national holidays, so they’re omitted here.

---
